title: Check the Amadeus test connection and set up Stripe test payments
summary: What provisioning connected for a new OTA (a test office of the Velexis Amadeus pool, a Stripe connection in Velexis mode), how both look in the portal and the platform admin, and how to make Stripe test payments work locally with the Stripe CLI.
prerequisites: An active OTA of your own ([[journey:signup-and-provision]]) and the platform admin signed in ([[journey:run-the-stack]]).
For the Stripe steps: a Stripe account in test mode, the Stripe CLI and your own `sk_test_…`/`pk_test_…` keys (never live keys).

steps.title: The OTA's Amadeus page
steps.actions: Open your OTA → **Amadeus**. Read the test connection. As owner or admin, change one connection setting (default, queuing or owner office, ticketing defaults or monitored queues), save, then reload.
steps.expect: The **Amadeus** page shows one card per environment, test first, through the Velexis test account, status active, with the assigned `DEV1A…` office. Owners and admins get the settings form; finance members read the same values without a form. With `FEATURE_LIVE_SWITCH` off (the default) there is no live access section; with it on, an owner on `early_access` (no live mode) gets no request button. Saved settings stay after a reload.
steps.data: `SELECT environment, status, credential_source, office_ids, default_office_id, queuing_office_id, owner_office_id, monitored_queues FROM platform.supplier_connections WHERE tenant_id = 'ten_…';`. A settings change writes the audit row `amadeus.settings_updated` and publishes `vx:invalidate {type: "connection"}` (watch with `redis-cli -a dev_redis SUBSCRIBE vx:invalidate`).

steps.title: The Velexis Amadeus account and the office pool
steps.actions: Open **Amadeus → Accounts** and **Amadeus → Offices**; filter offices by status. Open your OTA on **Tenants** and find its connection.
steps.expect: The test account is active with its last verification time; the pool shows the offices `assigned` to `demo` and to your OTA and the rest `available`. The tenant page names the same office as the portal.
steps.data: `SELECT office_id, status, assigned_tenant_id FROM platform.amadeus_offices WHERE status <> 'available';`

steps.title: See the shared Amadeus token and rate buckets
steps.actions: Run one search on your storefront, then list the Amadeus keys in Redis: `REDISCLI_AUTH=dev_redis redis-cli -n 0 --scan --pattern 'amadeus:*'` and `--pattern 'rl:amadeus:*'`.
steps.expect: One `amadeus:token:<credId>:test` key (encrypted value) with a TTL a minute shorter than the token's lifetime, shared by the demo OTA and yours (same Velexis credentials). Rate-limit keys `rl:amadeus:cred:…` and `rl:amadeus:ten:<tenantId>:test` with a TTL of about 2 s.
steps.data: `SELECT operation, http_status, duration_ms, office_id FROM tenant_<key>.supplier_requests ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 5;` shows the token-backed calls with your office.

steps.title: The OTA's Payments page and card statement descriptor
steps.actions: Open **Payments**. Read the connection (Velexis mode, test). As owner or admin, change the card statement suffix: try `-BAD`, a 23-character text and `ÅSE TRAVEL`, then `ACME TRAVEL`.
steps.expect: Velexis mode is shown as active for test. Invalid suffixes are refused at the field with the rule's message: `-BAD` and `ÅSE TRAVEL` "Use only the letters A to Z, digits and spaces: no accents, punctuation or other symbols.", 23 characters "Use at most 22 characters." (rules: 2 to 22 characters, letters A to Z, digits and spaces, at least one letter, starting with a letter or digit). `ACME TRAVEL` is saved ("The card statement suffix is saved. …") and shown after a reload. The **Payout account** and **Settlements** entries appear only with `FEATURE_SETTLEMENTS=true`.
steps.data: `SELECT provider, environment, account_mode, capture_mode, status, statement_descriptor_suffix FROM platform.payment_provider_connections WHERE tenant_id = 'ten_…';`

steps.title: Read the payment configuration the storefront receives
steps.actions: Open your storefront with DevTools → Network and inspect the answer of `/api/v1/storefront`.
steps.expect: Its payment section names the account mode `velexis`, merchant "Velexis on behalf of `<OTA name>`" and the descriptor; `publishableKey` is the value of `STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY_TEST`. With the committed dummy key the card method cannot work; no secret key ever appears.

steps.title: Give the OTA backend real Stripe test keys and start the listener
steps.actions: Put `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY_TEST=sk_test_…` and `STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY_TEST=pk_test_…` in `ota/backend/.env.local`. Run `stripe login` once, then `bash tools/dev/stripe-listen.sh --only ota`. Copy the printed `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET_VELEXIS_TEST=whsec_…` into `ota/backend/.env.local` and restart the OTA backend.
steps.expect: The script prints `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET_VELEXIS_TEST=whsec_…`, then `==> [ota] stripe listen --forward-to localhost:4000/webhooks/stripe/velexis/test` and the Stripe CLI's own lines prefixed `[ota] ` (its `> Ready! …` line among them). It stops with `ERROR: …` when `STRIPE_API_KEY` holds a live key or `/etc/velexis` exists. After the restart `/api/v1/storefront` carries your real publishable key.

steps.title: Send a webhook without a tenant
steps.actions: Run `stripe trigger payment_intent.succeeded` and watch the listener and the OTA API log.
steps.expect: The listener shows `[ota] … --> payment_intent.succeeded` and `<-- [200]`. The OTA API logs the event as one of an unknown tenant (no `velexis_tenant_id` metadata) and acknowledges it, so Stripe does not retry it.
steps.data: No new `payment_events` row in any tenant schema.

steps.title: Optional: platform billing with Stripe Billing
steps.actions: Only to test M5 billing: as platform admin give a public plan a Stripe test Price (**Billing → Plans**; `early_access` has none). Set `FEATURE_STRIPE_BILLING=true`, a real test `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` and the `STRIPE_BILLING_WEBHOOK_SECRET` printed by `bash tools/dev/stripe-listen.sh --only billing` in `platform/backend/.env.local`; restart API and worker; create a new OTA on that plan.
steps.expect: Create OTA now redirects to Stripe Checkout (a plan without a Stripe Price answers `422 PLAN_NOT_AVAILABLE`); after paying with `4242 4242 4242 4242` you come back to `/otas/<id>/setup?checkout=success` and provisioning starts once `checkout.session.completed` has been processed.
